svg.title: A 4-year-old hospitalized for 3 days has started wetting the bed and asking for a bottle, although he was fully toilet trained at home. His mother is embarrassed and asks the nurse what she is doing wrong. Which response by the nurse is best?
svg.desc: Regression under stress is normal , and the nursing action is to normalize it to the parents rather than treat it. Retraining him with reminders and fluid restriction is tempting because it looks like active teaching, but it treats an expected stress response as a problem and adds shame.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Toddler & Preschooler
Read the situation
A 4-year-old hospitalized for 3 days has
started wetting the bed and asking for a
bottle, although he was fully toilet
trained at home.
What fits here
"Regression like this is a normal reaction
to the stress of being in the hospital,
and it usually fades once he is home in
his own routine."
Why it fits
Regression under stress is normal , and
the nursing action is to normalize it to
the parents rather than treat it.
Retraining him with reminders and fluid
restriction is tempting because it looks
like active teaching, but it treats an
expected stress response as a problem and
adds shame.
